definitions.explanation: The reduction or elimination of nuclear weapons by one or more countries, typically pursued through international treaties and negotiations.

examples.japanese: {核軍縮|かくぐんしゅく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{目指|めざ}す→目指す：10528_mezasu⟧。
⟦{両国|りょうこく}→両国：10010_ryoukoku⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{核軍縮|かくぐんしゅく}⟦について→〜について：03103_nitsuite⟧⟦{話|はな}し{合|あ}った→話し合う：02396_hanashiau⟧。
examples.english: The two countries held talks on nuclear disarmament.

examples.japanese: {核軍縮|かくぐんしゅく}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{実現|じつげん}→実現：03276_jitsugen⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{向|む}けた→向ける：02306_mukeru⟧⟦{国際的|こくさいてき}→国際的：06457_kokusaiteki⟧な⟦{努力|どりょく}→努力：03490_doryoku⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{続|つづ}け→続く：00903_tsuzuku⟧られて⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: International efforts continue to work toward the realization of nuclear disarmament.

notes:
Composed of ⟦{核|かく}→核：13127_kaku⟧ (nuclear) and ⟦{軍縮|ぐんしゅく}→軍縮：24085_gunshuku⟧ (disarmament, military reduction). A standard term in news reports and diplomatic discussions about nuclear weapons and international security. Japan, as the only country to have suffered atomic bombings, historically takes an active rhetorical stance in favor of {核軍縮|かくぐんしゅく}, and the word appears frequently in news coverage of international summits and treaty negotiations.
